action: Bitdefender advises avoiding software downloads from social-media ads, refusing administrator prompts with an unclear purpose, and treating an unexpected "managed by your organization" browser message as a red flag.
date_note: Date of the BleepingComputer and Hackread reports of Bitdefender's findings; the pages give no earlier disclosure day. Bitdefender says it identified a malicious ad on October 16.
exec: Bitdefender says SYS010 malware, spread by Facebook ads, can read Gmail and Outlook mail in Chrome and gather Meta business account data.
geo_basis: no victim or place stated; global ad campaign
plain: Bitdefender says ads on Facebook offering free animated wallpapers install malware on Windows PCs. It enrols browsers in attacker-controlled management and adds an extension that can reach email and Meta business accounts.
summary: Bitdefender Labs, which tracks the campaign as SYS010, says Meta ads lure Windows users with free animated wallpapers that impersonate Wallpaper Engine and Lively Wallpapers. According to BleepingComputer's report of the research, the malware enrols browsers in attacker-controlled management to force-install a data-stealing extension that can reach Gmail and Outlook messages in Chrome. Bitdefender found a malicious ad on October 16; the reports name no actor.
title: Bitdefender: SYS010 malware spread by Facebook wallpaper ads abuses browser management to reach Gmail and Outlook

validation.note: BleepingComputer and Hackread each report Bitdefender's SYS010 findings; Bitdefender's own post was not read, so no primary source.
